accuracy.evidence: Parallelogram A = b × h and triangle A = ½ × b × h with h the perpendicular height (NC 2014 Y6 measurement, CCSS 6.G.A.1). Every number in the lab is checked on the 1 cm grid: the 8 × 5 parallelogram with a 2-square overhang becomes the 2..10 × 0..5 rectangle (40 squares); the lean step keeps base 8 and height 5 while the slanted side reads √(s² + 25) (6.4 cm at s = 4); the height step uses a 3-4-5 slant, so base 6 × height 4 = 24 and 6 × 5 = 30 is the visible wrong answer; the turned copy maps (x, y) → (8 − x, 4 − y) and lands exactly on the parallelogram (0,0)(6,0)(8,4)(2,4); the apex step keeps ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 for every top-corner position; build needs b × h = 36. Challenge answers re-computed: 20, 28, 20, 6, 12. Parameterised items checked at range corners (p2 k·h for k 2..7, m6 2k with area k·h).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented errors for this topic (NCETM Y6 measurement guidance; Ryan & Williams' children's mathematical errors): using the slant side (step 3 prediction option, challenge tag 'slant' on Q2 and Q3, m3), forgetting to halve a triangle (tag 'nohalf', m3), halving a parallelogram (tag 'halfpg', m2 explanation), adding base and height (tag 'add'), area changing when a shape is sheared (step 2 prediction, m4), the base including the overhang of an obtuse triangle (tag 'outside', m8), and the triangle being 'equal' or 'a third' (step 4 prediction, tags 'equal'/'third', m5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtripar is built on this topic's own dissections: a translate-the-cut-triangle move, a shear of the top edge, a choice between a slanted side and a perpendicular, a 180° rotation of a congruent triangle about the midpoint of a side, a vertex sliding parallel to the base, and a b × h = 36 search. flagtiles counts unit squares, flagcover is about what area means and flagarea estimates curved areas; none rearranges shapes. The 6-shingle gate passes against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees each fact happen before it is named: the readout says 'squares covered: 40' before and after the slide; the area stays 40 cm² while the side label climbs from 5 cm to 6.4 cm and beyond; choosing the 5 cm side shows '6 × 5 = 30? But it covers 24 squares'; the dashed copy only becomes '24 cm² ÷ 2 = 12 cm² each' once it has been turned and joined; the apex can be dragged anywhere on the 4 cm line and the area never moves; the build target forces them to double 18 to 36. Each task then closes with the one-line rule.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with a tempting wrong option that the lab disproves: area 'gets bigger' when the triangle moves (count stays 40), 'grows, because the sides are longer' when leaning (stays 40 cm² as the slant grows), multiply by 'the slanted side' (gives 30, but 24 squares are covered), and the triangle is 'a third' or 'the same size' (two copies fill it exactly). The apex step prediction 'gets bigger' is disproved by the fixed 12 cm² readout.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, each with two wrong answers tied to a named slip and its own message: 'nohalf' (that is the whole parallelogram, halve it), 'add' (area multiplies rows by squares; adding gives a length), 'slant' (the slanted side is longer than the right-angle height), 'halfpg' (only triangles are halved), 'subtract' (height = area ÷ base; subtracting mixes cm² and cm), 'tri' (doubling is for triangles), 'outside' (the base is the 4 cm side it stands on), 'equal' and 'third' (two copies fill it).

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes: learner kid text FK 3.0 (limit 6.5) and adult text FK 6.1 (limit 9.5). Kid paragraphs use short sentences with the precise terms the topic needs (parallelogram, parallel, base, perpendicular height, right angle, cm²), each explained where it first appears. Canvas readouts are 15–18 px dark text on white pills; buttons say what they do (Slide the triangle across, Lean right, Use the 4 cm dashed line, Base +1).

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases, explanation overlap under 12% with every lesson). Kid paragraphs: parallelogram to rectangle; base × height with a worked 8 × 5 and units; height versus slanted side; two triangles make a parallelogram with a worked 12 × 7. Adult paragraphs: curriculum link and why the formulae follow from the rectangle; base/height pairs and the outside height; named common mistakes; what each lab step does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots on iPhone 13 (390 px) in light and dark themes before and after Show me on all 7 steps. The first pass had a lot of empty space above the grid and the step-4 readout ('Parallelogram 6 × 4 = 24 cm², so one triangle = 12 cm²') clipped at 390 px; the grid is now centred vertically and the narrow readout is '24 cm² ÷ 2 = 12 cm² each'. Labels sit on white pills inside the canvas; buttons wrap two per row and meet the 44 px touch size.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button twin: Slide the triangle across / Slide it back, Lean left / Lean right, Use the 5 cm side / Use the 4 cm dashed line, Turn the copy and join it, Move corner left/right, Base ±1 and Height ±1 (each with an aria-label naming the change). speak() sets the canvas aria-label and the live description after every action and each challenge question includes all its numbers in text. walk.cjs: all 6 tasks complete with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, challenge shown, axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes, no console errors.
